root_cause_analysis: The supported public question contains an explicit GMV surface: 'Why did social GMV fall on June 1 after the weekend campaign change?'. Round 16 predictions correctly expected metric_id=gmv, but the eval stream fataled with typed METRIC_NOT_FOUND for eval-result-LG01_gmv_lagged_social before any trace artifact or eval-result.json was written. This indicates one transient LLM intent misclassification can escape LLMIntentPlanner as a semantic METRIC_NOT_FOUND. The current planner path does not perform a bounded typed retry for semantic METRIC_NOT_FOUND when the utterance has an explicit known metric surface, so the whole eval dies before the normal trace/scorer path can produce case evidence. The fix must not substitute a default metric or silently degrade; it should retry the core intent parse under explicit typed constraints and then fail fast with METRIC_NOT_FOUND if the retry also cannot resolve the persisted metric metadata.

proposed_fix.description: Add a bounded typed retry in LLMIntentPlanner for semantic METRIC_NOT_FOUND when the question contains an explicit persisted metric surface such as GMV. The retry should re-run the core parser with a stricter metric-resolution instruction, assert the resolved metric exists in metadata, and preserve fail-fast METRIC_NOT_FOUND if the retry still fails. Add regression coverage proving explicit GMV resolves and unknown metrics still raise typed METRIC_NOT_FOUND.
proposed_fix.estimated_impact: Restores eval completion for LG01_gmv_lagged_social and reduces harness-fatal parser variance on explicit-metric questions without introducing default-provider or default-metric fallback behavior.
